equity_bridge.item: Series A 5.9% non-cumulative perpetual preferred (MassMutual), post 26-Oct-2026 repurchase
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q note 13 subsequent events: $1.5bn of $2.5bn repurchased at 112.5%; $1.0bn liquidation preference remains. Deducted at par; the two negotiated repurchases (116%, 112.5%) suggest a takeout premium of ~$125m more.

equity_bridge.item: Equity-method investments (incl. 49% Invesco Great Wall) at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q investments note; IGW earnings excluded from the flows, so its value enters here. Seed/deferred-comp hedge investments are excluded (they offset compensation liabilities).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: GAAP operating revenue CAGR (FY2020-25 0.7%, FY2022-25 1.8%) understates the 2026 step-up from QQQ fee capture and AUM growth; base path decelerates 5.5% -> 3.0%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.5% 3y, -2.7% 5y) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR: book value was cut by the FY2023 ($1.25bn) and FY2025 ($1.79bn) non-cash intangible impairments and the $240m preferred-repurchase premium, not by operating losses. EPS CAGRs are undefined because GAAP diluted EPS was negative in FY2025 (-1.60) and FY2023 (-0.73); adjusted diluted EPS rose 1.51 -> 1.71 -> 2.03 (FY2023-25).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - SBC (- withholding taxes where disclosed). Reported OCF is noisy (CIP investment purchases/sales and Q1 bonus timing run through it): FY2022 owner FCF ~404 vs FY2025 ~1,337, so the 3-year FCF CAGR of ~50% is a trough-to-normal artefact, not a trend. SBC has fallen (FY2020 188.5 -> FY2025 80.0) while cash comp stayed ~2.0bn, so the SBC-adjusted CAGR is not below reported.

scenario_narratives.base: Markets compound mid-single digits, positive organic flows led by ETFs/index, QQQ, private markets and the China JV, partly offset by 2-3%/yr fee-yield compression; net revenue +5.5% in 2027 fading to 3%; pre-SBC EBITDA margin ~39.5-40%.
scenario_narratives.bull: QQQ open-end conversion and ETF/private-markets momentum plus a continuing equity rally; operating leverage lifts the margin to 43%; growth 9% fading to 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Equity drawdown from record AUM (-10% net revenue in 2027) against a sticky comp base, renewed active outflows from the impaired U.S. retail mutual-fund franchise and accelerating passive fee compression; margin 34-36%, growth 2-3%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Invesco is valued as a fee stream on AUM: net revenue (ex pass-through distribution costs and ex the Great Wall gross-up) grown with markets plus flows minus fee compression, a pre-SBC EBITDA margin near the company's adjusted operating margin, SBC and withholding taxes fully expensed, and the remaining MassMutual preferred and new term-loan debt deducted. The FY2025 GAAP loss is a non-cash intangible impairment and is not extrapolated.
key_risks_to_valuation: Market beta: revenue tracks AUM, and 2026 earnings are on record AUM - a drawdown compresses both revenue and margin
Fee-yield compression from active-to-passive migration (net revenue yield 25.4bps FY2024 -> 21.5bps Q3-2026, partly QQQ mix)
Further impairment of U.S. retail mutual-fund management contracts (non-cash, but a signal of franchise decay)
Leverage re-added: $1.5bn term loan to retire preferred lifts net debt to ~$2.0bn
MassMutual's board seat and consent rights constrain corporate actions
China JV (Invesco Great Wall) regulatory and fee risk; valued at book in the bridge

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 21.82-33.66
data_sources.financials: IVZ 10-K FY2025 (income statement, cash flow, non-GAAP reconciliation, impairment note); 10-Q Q3-2026 (balance sheet, debt note, subsequent events, 9M non-GAAP reconciliation); IVZ_Metrics.csv / IVZ.duckdb kpis
data_sources.qualitative: IVZ_Analysis.json not yet available at build time; narratives drawn from 10-K/10-Q MD&A

inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 10-Q weighted average diluted common shares (452.5m; includes unvested restricted stock with dividend rights). Period-end common shares outstanding were 439.5m excluding unvested awards. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. withholding taxes on net-share settlement) is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: common share-based compensation expense $80.0m plus $23.6m paid to meet employees' withholding tax obligations on share vestings (financing activities); no combined figure published. 9M-2026 runs higher: SBC $91.9m + withholding $40.2m, hence the 3.3% forward path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Cost of equity 11.0% = 4.3% UST10y + 1.35 beta x 5.0% ERP (asset managers carry above-market beta through AUM-linked revenue and operating leverage). Pre-tax debt ~5.9% (term loans SOFR+, 5.375% 2043 notes), 4.5% after tax, ~17% of capital; perpetual preferred 5.9%, ~6%. WACC ~9.5%, identical across scenarios (risk charged once, in the scenario paths and weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (offices) left inside adjusted operating expenses (property, office and technology); lease liabilities NOT added to net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated investment products (CIP) and their NCI are excluded from the flows using the company's own CIP adjustment; Invesco Great Wall (49% China JV, which management grosses up to 100% in Net revenues/Adjusted operating income) is EXCLUDED from the flows and the Invesco equity-method carrying value is added in the equity bridge instead - charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route). Routing: an asset manager is an operating fee business (fees on AUM, light capex, no deposit funding, no fair-value earnings) - not a bank, insurer, REIT or LIC row, so owner-FCF applies; AUM/fee-yield dynamics are expressed through the revenue growth and margin paths. No prior DCF and no MEMORY entry; first valuation. REVENUE BASIS: 'Net revenues' as defined by Invesco (GAAP operating revenues less pass-through third-party distribution, service and advisory costs, plus the CIP fee elimination) but EXCLUDING the 100% Invesco Great Wall gross-up. FY2025: 6,377.1 - 2,127.1 + 44.5 = 4,294.5. FY0 is FY2026E = 9M-2026 net revenues ex-IGW 3,600.9 (3,975.1 - 374.2) plus a Q4 run-rate ~1,250 = ~4,850 (+13%, driven by QQQ's conversion to an open-end ETF on 20-Dec-2025, which moved QQQ fees into Invesco's revenue, and AUM up 19% y/y). FY0 is set to FY2026E rather than FY2025 because the Sep-2026 balance sheet already reflects nine months of 2026 cash generation (debt paid down, buybacks); projecting FY2026 as year 1 against that balance sheet would count those flows twice. Q4-2026 cash is omitted (small conservatism). FY2025 LOSS NORMALISED: GAAP operating loss of -695.7 is entirely a $1,794.9m non-cash impairment of indefinite-lived intangibles (acquired U.S. retail mutual fund management contracts, OppenheimerFunds), plus the $240m premium on the preferred repurchase below the line; adjusted operating income was +1,557.8 (33.4% margin). Nothing of the impairment is projected. MARGIN BUILD FY2026E: adjusted operating income ex-IGW 9M 1,260.9 (1,497.0 - 236.1) + Q4 ~475 = ~1,736 (35.8% of net revenue ex-IGW); + depreciation ex intangible amortisation ~97 + SBC expense ~120 = pre-SBC EBITDA ~1,953 = 40.3%. Deferred-comp market valuation changes are excluded per the company (economically hedged). AUM DISCONTINUITY: from Dec-2025 QQQ AUM moved into long-term, management-fee-earning AUM and net revenue yield fell (25.4bps FY2024 -> 21.5bps Q3-2026) on that mix shift; no AUM-based driver is used, revenue is modelled on the consistent net-revenue line instead. CAPITAL STRUCTURE (pro forma at 2026-09-30 for the 26-Oct-2026 subsequent event): debt 1,281.3 + new $1,500m five-year term loan = 2,781.3; cash 965.5 less the $187.5m (12.5%) repurchase premium = 778.0; Series A 5.9% non-cumulative perpetual preferred falls from $2.5bn to $1.0bn and is deducted in the equity bridge at liquidation preference. CIP cash/debt excluded. No interest income stripped: the company is net debt. Buybacks: FY2025 $123.6m treasury purchases incl. withholding, 9M-2026 $194.6m - a repurchaser, so the flat count is funded.
inputs.price_volatility_note: Regular-session close; not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: A 2027 equity drawdown from record AUM cuts net revenue ~10% while a ~$2bn comp-heavy cost base is sticky; active fundamental equity and fixed-income outflows (the franchise just written down by $1.8bn) resume and passive fee compression accelerates as QQQ competes on price. Margin resets to 34-36% and growth never recovers above 3%.

base.narrative: Markets compound mid-single digits, organic flows stay positive (ETF/index, QQQ, private markets, China JV) and fee-yield compression of ~2-3%/yr offsets part of it; net revenue grows 5.5% in 2027 off the elevated exit-2026 AUM and fades to 3%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin holds ~39.5-40% (FY2026E 40.3% was flattered by strong markets).

bull.narrative: QQQ's open-end conversion keeps paying (fee capture plus marketing-led share gains vs SPY/VOO-style rivals), ETF and private-markets flows accelerate, and equity markets extend the 2026 rally; Alpha platform and fundamental-equities restructuring deliver operating leverage, taking the margin to 43%. Freed from the preferred dividend, buybacks rise.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: FY2026 earnings sit on record AUM after a strong market year and an asset manager's operating leverage makes a market drawdown hit owner FCF hard; the active franchise has been impaired twice (2023, 2025). Base 50% is the central fee/AUM path. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both sustained market gains and continued share wins in a fee-compressing passive market.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
